### 2026-10-07 – # Started working on the macropad schematic.

**3h**

# Started working on the macropad schematic.

So to begin with i have TKL keyboard, which means no numpad for me :D.  I'm trying to learn blender and get better in it so I need some sort of device to use as numpad.  Why? Well for viewport navigation! There are some workarounds but nothing is as good as numpad and why buy new keyboard or buy separated numpad when you can build something like macropad! So that's exactly what i will be trying to do for this weeks project.

My idea is 12 key (4x3) key macropad (custom bindings), with rotary encoder (zooming/volume adjustment) and OLED display (songs, stats/telemetry, etc.).

Started with installing KiCad and spent a while (honestly a lot longer then I expected) just clicking around and getting familiar with interface. There i found out that i should do some proper research first. So I dove right into it. First i had to figure out how keyboard matrices work, because it turns out you can't just wire each switch to it's own pin.  You would run out of GPIO pins very quickly. Instead you use matrix system (rows x columns). You wire it into matrix and scan them. But there is a catch! Without diodes, pressing multiple keys at once causes "ghosting"  that means that MCU thinks that you are pressing keys that you're not pressing. Which is ofc problem :D. So that's why i had to add 1N4148 diodes to prevent this issue.

This article helped me a lot: https://docs.qmk.fm/how_a_matrix_works

After this i started drawing the matrix in KiCad. Placed 12 Sw_Push symbols in 4x3 grid with 1N4148 diodes. Guess what. I messed up at first! xD I had all diodes upside down, but thanks to my friend (was showing him my progress and it caught his eye) I fixed the issue before advancing to wiring. Pretty lucky huh?

![Screenshot 2026-10-07 at 10.09.09 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/pC9MgqhFa4fAOSZoioYCl67uOSWzXzxI/962ece852b55397c742e976f79da56d41ccd3cc6c03d43d71af4ac6ec4fc7a0e.png)
### *messed up so it's screenshot of screenshot, but here you can see part where I still had all my diodes flipped*

After that I started wiring it and i have made few mistakes here too. First mistake was pretty stupid honestly, I didn't realize that wires don't choose their path automatically. Sounds obvious, but my only experience with something similar to this was LOGO!soft comfort and in LOGO! wires can overlap etc.. Not in KiCad thought... But fortunately  I realized that and fixed it almost right away. (thank god i did, otherwise it would cause shortage. Second mistake came right after the first one, I've connected all of SWs and realized I can't connect diodes. ![Screenshot 2026-10-07 at 10.13.21 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/pC9MgqhFa4fAOSZoioYCl67uOSWzXzxI/dfd677499493a2a47fa939b7ec492424a6da8a325daaf5b05159c671cfa124c2.png)
### * messed up again, but here you can see I've fixed diodes and successfully messed up wiring xd*
So I did some research and found out about Labels,  Instead of physically wiring each pin you just create a label that counts as connection but leaves room for other cables while making the whole schematic A LOT cleaner.

![Screenshot 2026-10-07 at 3.54.29 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/pC9MgqhFa4fAOSZoioYCl67uOSWzXzxI/3e85956b87612ff3cc30a735ff9d8d8c980a60820652a68f6f06a4ce0538e0f1.png)

### *Finished key matrix with labels (ROW0, COL0, etc.)*

**tl;dr:** Installed KiCad, 4x3 matrix with diodes finished + learned about KiCad, ghosting and why i need diodes.

**Next up:** MCU setup, encoder and OLED.

### 2026-10-08 – ## Completing schematic

**2h**

## Completing schematic

I was supposed to write this yesterday, because I will be describing my evening session, but since it was really late when i finished describing my first (afternoon) session, I had gone to sleep.

Let's start, for the MCU I went with Pro Micro RP2040 (18 GPIO pins, usb-c and runs CircuitPython/KMK) . First problem was, that KiCad doesn't have a Pro Micro in its symbol lib. At first i found something with same "id" but it was raw chip with over 50 pins. After doing some research I found out that such a chip needs external flash, voltage regulator and crystal, which is waaaay too complex . So I had to do proper research on how to solve this, one option was to download it from internet and add it, but than I stumbled across some reddit page where I learned that I can use generic 2x12 pin connector and label the pins manually to match the Pro Micro pinout.

![Screenshot 2026-10-08 at 11.35.09 AM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/pC9MgqhFa4fAOSZoioYCl67uOSWzXzxI/e4415d0ba7089832d54da337b6faf75651c29785e2b8783431543349ac4aadcc.png)
### *2x12 pin connector with labeled pins*

Next thing was adding rotary encoder (EC11 with click --> adds more bindable options). Pins A and B for rotation, SW for the click + two 10k pullup resistors for A and B. Why pullups? Because without them the signal floats and rotation readings go crazy (floating is when pin is not connected to anything and it starts to pickup random noise, which makes readings go crazy)

![Screenshot 2026-10-07 at 8.34.16 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/pC9MgqhFa4fAOSZoioYCl67uOSWzXzxI/adb42156bb8212dec8a8c0fdf796317af9b3492c2966992a81064ffa7160f8e2.png)
### *Rotary Encoder*

For the OLED I  eventually chose a 2.08" SSD1322 over SPI. Why eventually? Honestly deciding which OLED to use was one of the hardest decisions so far, i wanted display that's big enough to cover the top right corner, while staying within budget and available pins. So calculation how big display I need and if I can afford it took pretty long time. So as I've already mentioned I decided to go with a 2.08" SSD1322, it's bigger then usual 0.96" OLEDs and needs 5 signal pins (MOSI, CLK, CS, DC, RST) instead of 2 for I2C. More wiring but better, since it's wider. Added it as 7 pin connector.

Ran ERC test at the end and finished with 4 errors for unused pins.

![Screenshot 2026-10-07 at 8.36.34 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/pC9MgqhFa4fAOSZoioYCl67uOSWzXzxI/4dd4465cc157f8eaa810c8dff28070f00b7ca4face789d3faea361554b7a94c9.png)
### *Finished ERC with 4 errors*

So I searched for a bit and found out that you have to mark unused pins. After I fixed it, it finished with 0 errors.

![Screenshot 2026-10-07 at 8.36.08 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/pC9MgqhFa4fAOSZoioYCl67uOSWzXzxI/5b0c298a6c35befd770c705708e4d6733d5aaebec4ae03909ec235b80dc91b6e.png)
### *Finished schematic + ERC test with no errors*

**tl;dr:** Full schematic done, Pro Micro RP2040, encoder with pullups, SSD1322 OLED and clean ERC
